For a 15.6-inch laptop, I'd recommend a screen extender with either two 15.6-inch displays or a single 14–15.6-inch display, depending on how portable you need it to be.

The biggest decision is whether you want two screens attached beside your laptop (three screens total) or just one extra screen.

What I'd look for

For a 15.6-inch laptop, pay attention to three things:

Mounting: A freestanding frame is usually more stable and easier on the laptop hinge than a heavy clip-on assembly.

Connectivity: USB-C must support video output (DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt), unless the extender uses another supported connection method.

Mac compatibility: Some MacBooks cannot natively drive two independent external monitors, so triple-screen systems may require DisplayLink.

chats.answer:
For a 15.6-inch laptop, I'd recommend a screen extender with a 15.6-inch Full HD IPS display, USB-C connectivity, and a sturdy mounting system.

There are two main styles worth considering:

Attachable screen extender

Clips onto your laptop, giving you two or three screens in one setup. Best for working while traveling.

Freestanding portable monitor

Sits beside your laptop. Usually lighter, more stable, and easier to position.

For most people, I'd favor a single attachable extender if portability is the priority, or a freestanding monitor if you'll use it mainly at a desk.
